questionText:
Given the following syntax directed translation rules:

Rule 1: $R \rightarrow AB \ \{B.i = R.i - 1; A.i = B.i; R.i = A.i + 1\}$
Rule 2: $P \rightarrow CD \ \{P.i = C.i + D.i; D.i = C.i + 2\}$
Rule 3: $Q \rightarrow EF \ \{Q.i = E.i + F.i\}$

Which ONE is the CORRECT option among the following?
options: Rule 1 is S-attributed and L-attributed; Rule 2 is S-attributed and not L-attributed; Rule 3 is neither S-attributed nor L-attributed
Rule 1 is neither S-attributed nor L-attributed; Rule 2 is S-attributed and L-attributed; Rule 3 is S-attributed and L-attributed
Rule 1 is neither S-attributed nor L-attributed; Rule 2 is not S-attributed and is L-attributed; Rule 3 is S-attributed and L-attributed
Rule 1 is S-attributed and not L-attributed; Rule 2 is not S-attributed and is L-attributed; Rule 3 is S-attributed and L-attributed
explanation:
Step-by-step Explanation:

Step 1: Understand S-attributed and L-attributed definitions.
• S-attributed SDD: Uses only synthesized attributes (attributes evaluated from children or constants).
• L-attributed SDD: Allows both synthesized and inherited attributes, provided that inherited attributes of a node depend only on its parent's attributes or attributes of its left-siblings. Every S-attributed SDD is also an L-attributed SDD.

Step 2: Analyze Rule 1 ($R \rightarrow AB$).
• $A.i = B.i$ defines an inherited attribute for $A$ based on $B$, which is to the right of $A$. This violates L-attributed rules.
• Since inherited attributes are used, it is also not S-attributed.
• Therefore, Rule 1 is neither S-attributed nor L-attributed.

Step 3: Analyze Rule 2 ($P \rightarrow CD$).
• $D.i = C.i + 2$ defines an inherited attribute for $D$ using $C.i$, which is a sibling to the left of $D$. This satisfies L-attributed rules.
• Since inherited attributes are computed, it is not S-attributed.
• Therefore, Rule 2 is not S-attributed and is L-attributed.

Step 4: Analyze Rule 3 ($Q \rightarrow EF$).
• $Q.i = E.i + F.i$ defines an attribute of the head $Q$ using attributes of its children $E$ and $F$ (synthesized evaluation).
• Since it uses only synthesized attributes, Rule 3 is S-attributed, and by definition, every S-attributed SDD is also L-attributed.

Hence, Option (C) is the correct choice.
